read_not_ported.jundot/omlx#3934 d2b6249f1c476184c1379f0: Already equivalent. omlx loops its native QSA prefill over query tiles (1024 -> 4096/2048/1024 rows by key count) inside one prefill chunk. mlx2 has no query-tile loop: QSAIndexer scores and selects for the whole prefill chunk in one pass and Attention dispatches NAX QSA (qwen4_qsa_nax.py, one grid over all rows) or dense-mask SDPA once per chunk, so the tile is the prefill chunk, 8192 rows in the Flash-Next profile since 623b6975 (triage-20260925: 2048 -> 8192 is -9..11% prefill at 16K/64K). No port and no A/B.
read_not_ported.jundot/omlx#3890 f9424f9327eb665cef9e358: Already equivalent. omlx's fused decode prework gated on an oQe (bits, group) allow-list for in_proj_* and out_proj. mlx2's admit_qwen4_fused_gdn_decode reads the projected qkv/z/b/a activations, not the projection storage, so any in-projection recipe reaches the kernel; the fused in-projection table concatenates any homogeneous quantized quartet and falls back to four calls otherwise; the optional out-proj epilogue (fused_outproj) is q4/g64-only and refuses with a reason to the stock out_proj.
read_not_ported.jundot/omlx#3873 2416093953eec14944d84b0: Not applicable. It enables an FP16-compute Flash-Next (target M2 Ultra). mlx2 serves the bf16 artifact on M5; its PLE sidecar decodes bf16 bits (qwen4_ple_nvme.py) and the fused GroupRMSNorm admits bf16 only, refusing with a reason. There is no FP16 Flash-Next artifact or profile to carry it.

modifications: #3912: kernel sources carried from omlx with renamed kernels. One arithmetic adaptation: the input sums in load_vector/load_vector_safe cast each element to float before adding, as the lab MLX fork in the mlx2 venv does since 2d6705923 (mlx 39400a0d4). With omlx's verbatim 0.32.2 transcription the gate/up rows differed from gather_qmm in ~78% of elements and were ~3x further from an fp32 reference (routed-micro-verbatim-header.json); after the adaptation both kernels are bit-identical to MLX on this venv.

#3912: the omlx monkey-patch of mlx-vlm Qwen3_5MoeSparseMoeBlock.__call__ (which also required omlx's fused router) is replaced by a hook in mlx2's FusedGateUpSwitchGLU; routing stays mlx2's own (stock or the opt-in qwen4_moe_router).

#3912: split into two modes. gate_up runs only the gate+up/SwiGLU kernel and keeps whatever down path the block runs (mlx2's tile4 fused down in the Flash-Next profile), so it is bit-identical to the current default. two_launch is the literal omlx pairing; its down kernel reproduces the stock gather_qmm + (x*scores).sum tail, not mlx2's tile4 fused down (fp32 accumulation), so it changes numerics relative to the Flash-Next default.

#3912: admission is a structural check with a reason (counted as routed_decode_fallbacks); multi-token (sorted-gather) forwards decline quietly; streamed expert tables (no resident weight) decline; no first-launch self-disable (a kernel error propagates).
#3912: default off; selected by FlashNextPolicy.moe_routed_decode (off | gate_up | two_launch), which enters the environment and receipts only when not off.

#3935: omlx keeps the MTP head resident automatically whenever MTP and offload are both on. mlx2 makes it an explicit, default-off moe_expert_streaming.mtp_resident flag (present in the resolved policy only when true); kept tables are excluded from the per-layer capacity plan and listed in plan.resident_paths.

2026-09-30 (original mlx2, no new source mined; found while assessing jundot/omlx#4113 @1335263e): the MoE block's stock expert branch called the switch module without scores, so a selected two_launch silently ran gate+up only while routed_decode_calls rose. The block now passes the scores for a one-token two_launch forward with variant='stock'; a declined admission runs the same ops as before, so its output is bit-identical. New integer counters routed_decode_down_calls and routed_decode_degraded (a two_launch call without scores) appear in the Flash-Next routed_decode diagnostics. CPU tests in tests/test_omlx_fn_ports.py; the block test fails without the pass-through.
